post.yt_desc:
In fiscal 2026, Walmart kept about 3 cents of every dollar of revenue as net income: $22.3 billion on $713.2 billion, according to its 10-K. This video breaks down how Walmart beat everyone on price: Sam Walton's five-and-dime start, distribution centers, cross-docking, Retail Link and everyday low prices; the thin-margin math (24.2% gross margin, 20.9% operating expenses, about 4% operating margin); inventory that turns about 9.3 times a year; and the second engine of membership fees, nearly $6.4 billion in advertising and $150.4 billion in e-commerce sales. Full-year figures are fiscal 2026 (year ended January 31, 2026), with quarterly results through the quarter ended July 31, 2026; this video was made before Walmart reported its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, so those are not included.
